subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 19, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Hi Asha,

Following up on yesterday’s call: below is our proposed commitment language for the Runtime LTS channel (for Dedicated/Private). I’ve attached a short overview plus a draft addendum we can redline.

Proposed commitments (Runtime LTS channel):

1) Support window (per LTS branch)
- Redwood will provide patches for an LTS branch for 18 months from initial .0 release.
- During the support window, we will issue patch releases for security fixes, correctness/stability fixes, and narrowly-scoped performance/regression fixes.

2) Patch cadence
- Regular cadence: monthly patch release (targeting the last full week of the month).
- Out-of-band: critical security or severe correctness incidents may trigger an off-cycle patch.

3) Backport policy (what is eligible)
- Eligible: (a) security fixes, (b) correctness/stability fixes, (c) fixes for regressions introduced after the LTS cut, (d) performance regressions where we can demonstrate risk-controlled change and measurable improvement.
- Not eligible: feature work, refactors for code health only, or changes that materially alter scheduling semantics/behavior unless required to fix a correctness/security issue.

4) Release notes expectations
- Each LTS patch includes “enterprise-style” release notes: summary, impact, risk level (low/med/high), behavior changes, known issues, and mitigations.

5) Response times (non-SLA)
- For Severity 1 issues affecting production, we will engage same business day and determine whether an emergency LTS patch is warranted.

If you can confirm your target support window requirement (12/18/24 months) and whether you need a fixed day-of-month for patches (vs “last full week”), we can tighten the language.

Best,
Connor

—
Connor O'Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Runtime_LTS_Channel_Overview_v0.6.pdf
Attachment: Redwood_LTS_Support_and_Backport_Addendum_draft_v2.docx


From: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 19, 2025 at 1:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Connor,

Thanks. We reviewed internally.

Two items we need tightened before we can sign off:

1) Support window: 24 months is our standard for infrastructure dependencies. 18 months will force a branch move during our annual change freeze.

2) Patch cadence: “monthly / last full week” is too loose for our CAB calendar. We need either (a) a specific week of the month, or (b) a minimum notice period and a defined “no-change window” around our freeze.

Also, we’ll need the backport process spelled out: how we request a backport, who approves it, and what evidence we’ll see (test results, artifact hashes).

-Asha


From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 20, 2025 at 10:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Asha,

Understood. A few specifics (and a proposal):

Support window
- We can commit to 18 months of full support (security + correctness + approved perf/regression fixes).
- Additionally, we can offer a 6-month “security-only extension” for the same LTS line (i.e., 24 months total coverage, with the last 6 months limited to security patches and critical severity fixes). This helps customers align to annual upgrade windows while keeping the change surface very constrained late in the branch lifecycle.

Patch cadence / CAB planning
- We can target “2nd full week of each month” for regular LTS patches.
- Notice: we can provide release candidate notes at least 10 business days prior to GA for CAB review (content + known issues + risk level).
- Freeze: we can honor your change freeze windows for scheduled patches; we’d only publish out-of-band patches during freeze for critical security issues or Sev1 correctness issues, and only with explicit go/no-go from your designated approver.

Backport requests & evidence
- Request path: you can file via your Support channel (we’ll map it to a tracked issue) or via your TAM/CS contact; we’ll treat it as an “LTS backport request.”
- Approval: requires runtime owner approval + release engineering signoff; high-risk changes require SRE gate owner review.
- Evidence: we will provide test run links/summary, perf canary results where applicable, and artifact provenance (signed images + hashes) for the patch.

If the 18+6 structure works, I’ll update the addendum language to be explicit about what “security-only” means (and what’s excluded).

Best,
Connor


From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 20, 2025 at 12:23 PM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Connor,

18+6 may be workable.

Can you clarify a couple of operational points:

1) If a security issue appears in month 20, will the fix be backported to the same LTS line (security-only extension) or will you require moving to a newer branch?

2) What does “risk level” mean in the release notes? We need something we can pass to CAB without engineers having to decode internal jargon.

3) For backports: we need assurance that “performance improvements” don’t turn into functional behavior changes. For example, scheduler changes can affect per-tenant fairness and latency.

Thanks,
Daniel


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Nov 20, 2025 at 12:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

(Internal note)

Connor — for Daniel’s Q1, we should be explicit: during security-only extension, security fixes are backported to the same LTS line unless the fix is not technically safe/feasible without larger change. If infeasible, we should commit to (a) providing mitigations, and (b) providing a supported upgrade path with clear risk notes.

For Q2, define risk in customer terms (upgrade complexity, config changes, behavior changes, rollback confidence). Avoid wording that implies a formal SLA unless legal wants it.

-Naomi


From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 9:35 AM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Daniel,

Good questions—answers below.

1) Security issue in month 20 (security-only extension)
- Yes: our intent is to backport security fixes to the same LTS line during months 19–24.
- If a fix is not technically safe/feasible to backport without broad changes (rare, but possible), we will provide:
  (a) documented mitigations/workarounds, and
  (b) a supported upgrade recommendation with an explicit risk note and a prioritized support path.

2) “Risk level” definition (CAB-friendly)
We’ll define risk level in the release notes using customer-operational criteria:
- LOW: no behavior change expected; no config change; rollback is straightforward; limited blast radius.
- MEDIUM: potential behavior change in edge cases OR requires config/flag change; additional canary recommended; rollback supported but requires steps.
- HIGH: behavior changes likely OR touches scheduling/kernels in a way that could affect latency/fairness; requires extended canary; explicit go/no-go checklist.

3) Performance improvements vs behavior changes
Agreed. For LTS, “performance” backports are constrained:
- We only backport perf changes if they are narrowly scoped and do not change scheduling semantics.
- Any scheduler-related change (even if motivated by perf) will be treated as MEDIUM/HIGH and must include:
  - explicit statement of what does/does not change (fairness/priority/queuing),
  - measurable before/after perf results, and
  - a rollback plan.

I’m revising the addendum to reflect this language. Will send v3 early next week for your redlines.

Best,
Connor


From: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 24, 2025 at 8:19 AM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Connor,

Thanks — this is close.

We have two redlines that procurement will insist on:

1) Notice period: 10 business days is OK, but we need the notice to include a draft of the release notes (even if preliminary) and confirmation of the target release date.

2) Backport turnaround: we need a commitment that accepted Severity 1 issues will have a patch candidate within 5 business days (or an explicit written explanation why not).

Please send the updated addendum so we can route it.

-Asha


From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha.mehta@nimbusbank.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbusbank.com>, Procurement <procurement-it@nimbusbank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 26, 2025 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Runtime LTS commitments (support window + patch cadence) — Nimbus Bank

Asha,

Attached is the updated addendum draft (v3) with your two items addressed.

Edits incorporated:

Notice period (CAB)
- Redwood will provide at least 10 business days’ notice prior to a scheduled LTS patch GA.
- Notice will include: (a) the target GA date, and (b) draft release notes (preliminary), with a final version published at GA.

Sev1 / emergency backport turnaround
- For Severity 1 issues determined to be caused by the runtime and eligible for LTS, Redwood will deliver either:
  (a) a patch candidate (RC) within 5 business days, or
  (b) a written explanation of the blocking constraint (e.g., reproducibility gap, upstream dependency, safety concern) plus mitigations and the next committed checkpoint date.

One nuance: we can’t commit that every Sev1 yields a patch candidate in 5 business days, because sometimes the safe action is a config mitigation + continued investigation rather than a rushed kernel/scheduler change. The language above is intended to cover that while still giving you a firm operational commitment.

If you’re ok with that framing, we’re ready for redlines.

Best,
Connor

—
Connor O'Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_LTS_Support_and_Backport_Addendum_draft_v3.docx
